subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What canonical inbound-media isolation boundary should OpenClaw enforce across agents and channels: account, resolved agent/session, tenant-aware scope, or explicit-share based access?
rationale: The issue is security-sensitive and any fix sets a durable storage, reference, staging, and sharing contract that code inspection alone cannot choose.

options.title: Define scoped contract first
options.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

options.title: Limit to account scoping
options.body: Implement the lower-friction account-based directory model while accepting follow-up work for non-1:1 account-to-agent and tenant cases.

options.title: Defer broad core change
options.body: Keep only channel-specific slices open until a maintainer sponsors the cross-channel media-isolation design.

recommendation.title: Define scoped contract first
recommendation.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest current routing signal across the central media/staging code and prior issue review.
